steps: Inspect & unpack
Check the crate and insert for damage; the log set ships separately. Confirm the hardware kit, detach the firebox from the pallet and remove the glass frame with the latch tool.

1. Inspect the shipping crate and insert for damage; contact the dealer immediately if any is found.
  2. The log set is shipped separately. Don't install it until directed.
  3. Confirm the Miscellaneous Hardware Kit packed in the firebox crate: Fuel Conversion Kit, LP · Fireplace Conversion Notice Plate · Rock Wool Ember Fibers · Safety Screen Barrier Guidelines.
  4. Remove the attachment bracket screws at each side of the base to detach the firebox from the pallet.
  5. Take the Latch Tool from the pallet. Pull each of the two spring latches out and up, pivot the top of the glass frame forward and lift it out of the bottom channel. Set the glass aside on a clean, secure surface.
  6. Pre-installation fit-up: set the firebox in its final position and level and plumb it with the four corner leveling bolts (max. 1/2" adjustment). Pull it back out and read the installation requirements before final assembly.
Leveling-bolt height affects the required minimum clearance to combustible top trim and mantel (p. 7). The latch tool is needed for later glass service: retain and store it in a secure location.
Prepare the fireplace & chimney
Clean the existing flue (a Level II inspection may be needed, per NFPA 211); the chimney must be sound, with no combustible construction. Never connect to a flue serving any other appliance.

Approved for a solid fuel-burning factory-built fireplace or a code-approved solid fuel-burning masonry fireplace with the minimum cavity in fig. 5.2.

  • Thoroughly clean the chimney flue. Depending on its previous use, a Level II inspection may be necessary (NFPA 211).
  • Don't install into a damaged chimney or one containing combustible construction materials; make repairs first. Clean-outs must be accessible and fit properly.
  • Don't remove bricks or mortar. Masonry or steel may be removed from the smoke shelf and damper frame area for the liner if that doesn't weaken the structure or reduce protection for combustibles.
  • If the fireplace was modified, anchor the metal Fireplace Conversion Notice Plate to the back wall of the firebox where it will be seen if the insert is removed.

Factory-built fireplaces

  • Remove glass doors, screen rails, screen mesh and fuel grates; smoke shelves, shields and baffles may be removed if mechanically fastened. Keep them for possible re-installation.
  • Don't cut out any sheet metal parts of the fireplace.
  • No gas access inlet? An access hole of 1 1/2" or less may be drilled through the lower sides or bottom of the firebox; seal it with noncombustible insulation once the gas supply is in.
  • Remove the damper assembly (two 3" liners must pass through the damper area), any screen or door assembly, and the ash lip if needed so the insert sits flat.
  • Attach the fireplace conversion notice to the back of the fireplace.
The gas line to the firebox should only be installed by a qualified or licensed plumber or gas fitter (p. 12).
Vent liners & adaptor

Drop a pair of listed 3" flexible aluminum liners from the termination kit and trim them to hang about 18 3/4" from the fireplace floor. Facing the insert, intake collar on the left, exhaust on the right; secure with sheet metal screws or duct clamps.

Masonry fireplace (section 6.1)

  1. Measure the chimney height to the fireplace opening and decide whether both liners will run to the top. In Canada both must run full length and connect to the unit and the termination kit.
  2. Cut both liners; label both ends of the exhaust liner.
  3. Attach the liners to the chimney termination kit, drop them down the chimney and rest the kit on top. Seal it to the flue with high temperature sealant and secure the direct vent cap.
  4. Inside, fully extend the liners and trim so the ends hang approximately 18 3/4" from the fireplace floor.
  5. Intake not attached to the termination kit: run it at least into the first flue tile, permanently seal the chimney flue from the room, and still fit a direct vent cap.
  6. Push the Vent Adaptor off the unit to the rear, connect both liners, set the insert half-way into the fireplace (no backer plate) and start the adaptor onto the firebox. Secure with sheet metal screws or duct clamps: a good seal, but no sealant needed.

Factory-built (section 6.3)

Same liner sequence. If the intake isn't attached to the termination kit, install at least a 6 foot length of intake flex into the flue and a metal damper block-off plate with holes for both liners. Remove the Vent Adaptor lock screw, attach the liners by the EXHAUST ID on the panel, engage the panel on the vent manifold pins with the Latch Tool and refit the lock screw. Backer plates or the overlay must not block the fireplace's ventilation openings.

Avoid cross-venting: label the exhaust liner at both ends. Leaking vents can result in poor performance or draft reversal.
Gas line, leak & pressure test

Connect to the valve on the left side (min. 3/8" supply line; a 36" length of 3/8" flexible gas line is supplied) with a gas cock upstream, and leak-test with soapy water or a gas sensor. Check inlet (A) and manifold (B) pressure with a manometer.

• Supply line min. 3/8" diameter, or sized to deliver enough pressure to the valve at any input setting.
  • Where flexible gas lines aren't permitted, a 3/8" iron nipple and union is recommended.
  • Install the integrated gas cock in the supply line upstream of the valve (shut-off in the same room as the appliance).
  • Propane requires sealant specifically resistant to propane.
  • Leak test: open the supply valve and test with a soapy water solution or a digital gas sensor, never an open flame. Tighten or reconnect any leaking joint and retest.

Pressure test

Attach a manometer to the test points on the front of the valve: A inlet (supply), B manifold. Always test inlet pressure with the regulator control knob on HIGH and all other gas appliances in the residence on.

NG inlet5.0 – 7.0 in. WC
LP inlet11.0 – 14.0 in. WC
NG manifold1.2 – 3.8 in. WC
LP manifold2.9 – 11.0 in. WC
Don't allow inlet pressure to exceed 14.0" WC (or 1/2 PSIG): serious valve damage may result.
Massachusetts: installation by a licensed master or journeyman plumber or gas-fitter; a T-handle gas cock is required (248 CMR); see p. 2 for the carbon monoxide detector rules.
Fuel conversion / high altitude

The insert ships for natural gas; LP kit #158190 is included (#158191 converts back). An authorized Jøtul service technician swaps the burner injector, pilot orifice and regulator tower before the surround goes on or the insert goes in.

Complete before installing surround plates or placing the insert in the fireplace. Tools: 1/2" or 13 mm open end wrench or deep-well socket, Torx T20 driver, 1/4" nut driver, 7/16" open end wrench.

  1. Turn off the gas supply and disconnect electrical power.
  2. Remove the glass frame (Latch Tool), then the burner: lift its front edge off the pins and wiggle it forward off the main burner orifice, ideally with the air shutter fully closed.
  3. Burner injector: remove it from the brass fitting at the rear of the firebox with a 1/2" or 13 mm wrench and fit the kit injector. Don't over-tighten: it can damage the brass elbow and cause a leak.
  4. Pilot orifice: remove the pilot head and injector, fit the kit injector flared end down, and orient the head to project flame to the flame sensor and burner ports.
  5. Regulator tower: remove three screws, the original tower, rubber diaphragm and spring; fit the new tower with the screws provided.
  6. Apply the kit's conversion labels where a service technician will see them.
  7. Reinstall the burner level, front legs on the floor studs. Leak-check the pilot head, regulator tower and all joints (no open flame), then pressure test.
  8. Confirm the burner with Initial System Check steps 1-3 before fitting accessories, logs and surround.
Note: the kit contents list on p. 16 says Label A goes on the base of the valve compartment; the procedure's step 7 on the same page says to apply it to the right side compartment adjacent to the Rating Plate.

High altitude

Above 2000 feet, check with the gas supplier first: most derate the gas. If they don't, install High Altitude Adjustment Kit #158192 (NG) or #158187 (LP); orifices for 2000-4500 ft are #33 NG and 1.75 mm LP. Fill out the high altitude conversion label and apply it to the rating plate.
Optional remote or wall thermostat

Remote kit #224910: set the receiver box (4 AA) on the floor of the steel housing left of the gas valve and connect its leads to the valve terminal block. Wall thermostat #750003: 750 millivolt DC two-wire, min. 16 gauge wire, max. 35 feet.

Remote Control Kit #224910

  1. Put the 4 AA batteries in the receiver box and the 2 AAA batteries in the transmitter.
  2. Peel the film off the Velcro pad and set the receiver on the floor within the steel housing to the left of the gas control valve.
  3. Remove the Burner Control face plate (upper two #8 hex head screws).
  4. Connect the receiver leads to the valve terminal block (fig. 7.7).

Wall Thermostat #750003

  • Use only a 750 millivolt, DC two-wire circuit wall thermostat.
  • Minimum 16 gauge wire, up to a maximum length of 35 feet.
  • Same room as the heater, typically 5 feet off the floor, away from drafts.
  • Connect each lead to either of the two open terminal block connectors on the back of the control panel. Don't over-tighten.

Either control works with the burner switch at STAT and the pilot lit.
Backer plate
Install it before the insert goes into its final position, after the gas, vent and fuel conversion are complete. Choose a plate at least 1 inch larger than the fireplace opening.

The backer plate covers the opening between the insert shell and the fireplace walls. Standard plates: 16 gauge aluminized steel, Matte Black powder coat. Trimmable plates: 22 ga. aluminized steel, Matte Black paint, intended for flush-faced fireplaces.

158181 · 3-sided44" x 30"
158182 · 3-sided45" x 32"
158183 · 3-sided46" x 34"
158184 · 3-sided trimmable47-3/4" x 38"
158185 · 4-sided trimmable47-3/4" x 38"
  • Loosen the surround spacer screws. The plate's four hanger hooks engage the outer slots of the firebox brackets from behind (note the small ID hole above the slot).
  • Keep the firebox far enough out of the fireplace to fit the plate.
  • Tools: gloves and eye protection, a zip wheel or other sheet metal cutter for the trimmable plate, Phillips screwdriver.
Firebox panels & log set
Fit any optional panel kit first, then the log set in the order shown, using the ID number on the back of each log. Keep the pilot and burner carry-over ports clear.

Panel kits

158131 Black Reflective Glass · 158132 Traditional Red Brick · 158195 Brownstone Brick · 158133 Black Fluted.

  • The panels are very fragile; inspect each one and handle gently.
  • The rear panel rests on the rear burner skirt, flat against the back of the firebox; the side panels lock it in place.
  • Brick or fluted kits: left panel on the burner skirt, baffle on top, then the right panel.
  • Glass kit: wear the cotton gloves supplied, fit the retainer tabs at the upper front corners, set each side panel textured side in against a steel stand-off plate, and tighten the tab nuts with a 10mm wrench until secure. Over-tightening may damage the glass.

Log sets

Traditional 158153 · Beach Fire 158154 · Birch 158352. Install the logs in the manual's order, engaging the holes or notches under each log with the matching pins; the figures show the final arrangement.

Note: p. 3 lists Rock Wool Ember Fibers in the hardware kit and pp. 23 and 25 say to use rock wool fibers for the embers; p. 21 says to use the Ember Stones from the Miscellaneous Hardware bag (Ember Stones, 4 oz. are listed with set 158153), and p. 26 says Burner Ember Stones are included in the Misc. Kit.
Don't let logs, embers or rocks obstruct the pilot or burner carry-over ports. Frequently inspect the pilot area and keep it clear.
Surround overlay & heat shield

Hang the cast iron or steel overlay (safety barrier screen built in) on the inner slots of the firebox brackets, keeping a min. 1/2" (13 mm) air space. The optional Mantle Heat Shield #158201 slides over the backer plate.

• Both overlays ship fully assembled, including the integrated Safety Barrier Screen. The cast iron overlay is heavy: get help, and handle the enamel carefully.
  • The overlay hanger brackets engage the inner slots through the front of the firebox mounting brackets.
  • A minimum 1/2" (13 mm) air space must stay between the overlay and the backer plate or fireplace face. The backer plate hooks act as stand-offs; with no backer plate, fully insert the surround spacer screws on each firebox hanger bracket.
  • Mantle Heat Shield #158201: lower it onto the backer plate. Mantel clearances with the shield are in fig. 5.6.
  • Use only the surround options listed on p. 4; the insert is not for use with aftermarket glass doors.
Don't modify the hanger bracket positions or reduce the overlay air space: doing so may overheat the appliance and void the warranty.
Initial system check
Purge the line with the glass frame off, light the pilot and check all three pilot flames; then time burner light-off on LOW, cold and hot start, for full ignition within 4 seconds.

1. Purge: open the gas supply valve with the glass frame removed. The first lighting, or one after a long period of unuse, takes a few moments to clear air from the line.
  2. Pilot: light it per the lighting instructions. All three flames should project out of the pilot hood, blueish-yellow, extending approximately 1" over to the burner ports, thermopile and thermocouple; strong and steady, not fluttering or lifting, and fully engulfing the upper 1/4" of the thermocouple and thermopile. Adjust only with the pilot adjustment screw on the valve body (qualified gas technician).
  3. Light-off timing: in a cold flue, let the pilot burn 10-15 minutes first to establish draft. Set the regulator to LOW. Cold start: burner switch ON; full burner ignition within 4 seconds. Reinstall the glass frame. Hot start: after 5-10 minutes on, turn off, wait 2 minutes, turn on: again within 4 seconds, on low. Slower? See the light-off fault panel.
  4. STAT position for remote or wall thermostat; blower per section 8.2.

Flame picture / air shutter

Qualified service technician only. The primary air shutter is under the firebox at the center of the valve compartment; factory setting 1/2 open. Adjust in 1/8" - 1/4" increments, waiting a few minutes between: loosen the lock nut, push the handle in to decrease air or pull it out to increase, then retighten. Too little air gives very long yellow flames and soot; very blue, transparent or weak "anemic" flames mean too much air. Propane generally needs a less restricted setting than natural gas. No smoke or soot should be evident: check log placement first, then add air.

panels.title: Insufficient gas pressure
items: Small pilot flame → poor burner ignition and/or frequent burner outages
Little variation in flame picture between HI and LO
Not enough gas to support more than one appliance → nuisance outages or gas surges

panels.title: Excessive gas pressure
items: Permanent valve damage → complete appliance shut down
Pilot flame too large → flame sensor overheats and shuts down
Sooting from impingement and/or incorrect fuel to air mix

panels.title: Weak pilot or abnormal flame picture
items: Inlet good → remove the pilot hood (7/16" wrench), clean the head with emery cloth (no steel wool), blow out the line by depressing the valve knob as if lighting
Corrosion found, or problem persists → replace the pilot assembly

panels.title: Light-off over 4 seconds or hesitation
items: Loose media at the carry-over ports → remove the logs and rock wool there; gently clear the ports with a paper clip
Still slow → remove the burner and blow canned or compressed air through the venturi tubes (no brush or vacuum)
Still over 4 seconds → replace the burner

light.title: Lighting the pilot
light.html:
Your insert has a standing pilot you light by hand. Follow these steps exactly, or a fire or explosion may result, causing property damage, personal injury or loss of life. The steps are also on the rating plate.

  1. Smell all around the insert for gas, including next to the floor: some gas is heavier than air.
  2. Reach the lower controls, below the firebox.
  3. Turn the ON/OFF switch to OFF, or set the thermostat (if used) to its lowest setting.
  4. Check that the gas supply shut-off valve is open.
  5. Push the gas control knob in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF. The knob can't be turned from PILOT to OFF unless it's pushed in slightly. Don't force it.
  6. Wait five minutes to clear out any gas. If you then smell gas, stop and see Safety.
  7. Push the knob in slightly and turn it counterclockwise to PILOT.
  8. Push the knob all the way in and hold it. Right away, press the red igniter button repeatedly until the pilot lights. Keep holding the knob for about one minute, then let go. It should spring back and the pilot should stay lit. If it goes out, repeat steps 5 to 8.
  9. Turn the knob counterclockwise to ON.
  10. Turn the ON/OFF switch to ON, or set the thermostat to the temperature you want.
If the knob doesn't spring back when you let go, stop and call your service technician or gas supplier immediately. If the pilot won't stay lit after several tries, turn the knob to OFF and call your service technician or gas supplier.
Use only your hand to push in or turn the gas control knob. Never use tools. If the knob won't push in or turn by hand, don't try to repair it. Call a qualified technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.
Don't use the insert if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the insert and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

GI 645 DV MV only: with no call for heat for seven days, the pilot shuts off. Relight it with these steps.

onoff.title: Turning it on and off
onoff.html:
Once the pilot is lit, you run the fire from the lower controls.

  • Flames on or off: use the ON/OFF switch. With the switch off, the burner stops but the pilot stays lit.
  • Flame height: turn the regulator knob on the gas valve between HI and LO to set the fire's intensity and heat output.
  • STAT: this switch position hands control to an optional remote or wall thermostat.
Leaving the pilot on through the heating season keeps condensation (fog) on the glass to a minimum.

Shutting the gas off completely

  1. Turn the ON/OFF switch to OFF.
  2. Reach the lower controls.
  3. Push the gas control knob in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF. Don't force it.

GI 645 DV MV: if nothing calls for heat for seven days, the pilot goes out on its own and needs relighting by hand.

firstfire.title: Your first fires
firstfire.html:
The paint and log set on your insert finish curing with heat during the first fires. That gives off some odor and visible smoke. It's normal and temporary, and the fumes are non-toxic.

Before the very first fire

  • Ventilate: open doors and windows, and use a fan to move fresh air through the room.
  • Vacate: the fumes can be uncomfortable for babies, small children, pregnant women, the elderly, pets, and anyone with breathing difficulties.

The curing burn

After your installer has checked the burner at all heat levels, run the insert on a low setting for 2-4 hours, then on a high setting for another 2-4 hours.

Afterwards: clean the glass

A white, powdery film may form on the inside of the glass. Remove it with a non-abrasive household glass cleaner or warm water. Left on, it can permanently etch the glass.

Don't use ammonia-based cleaners on the glass.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Condensation is normal with gas fires: it forms each time the burner lights from cold and clears as the glass heats. Some buildup can also collect on the inside of the glass.

How to clean it

  1. Wait until the glass is cool. Never clean it hot.
  2. Wipe it with a dampened, soft cloth, then polish with a dry, soft towel. A specially formulated ceramic glass cleaner can be used too.
After the first few fires, clean off the white, powdery residue from the curing burner media. Left on, it can permanently etch the glass.
  • Don't use abrasive or ammonia-based cleaners, and take care not to scratch the glass.
  • Scratches weaken the glass. If you see any, have it replaced with Jøtul part 226451 by a licensed or qualified service person.
  • Never run the insert with the glass removed, cracked or broken.
  • Keep the glass frame latch tool that came with the insert in a safe place.

sounds.title: Sounds you may hear
sounds.html:
Creaking or pinging

The cast iron and steel parts expand and contract as they heat up and cool down. Those creaks and pings are natural thermal movement.

A soft "woof" or "thud"

A muffled woof or thud when the burner lights or goes out is normal. If it becomes unusually loud or disturbing, stop using the insert and call a qualified service technician.

A hum

The blower hums slightly on its low setting, and the sound grows as the fan speeds up.

Smoke or odor early on

During the first fires the paint is curing. Open windows and run a fan; see Your first fires.

A gas smell is not normal. Don't light anything, don't touch switches or use a phone in the building, and call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone.

remote.title: Remote control & wall thermostat
remote.html:
A remote control (kit 224910) and a wall thermostat (750003) are optional accessories. Either one turns the burner on and off for you while the pilot is lit.

  1. Set the burner switch to STAT.
  2. Light the pilot (see Light the pilot).
  3. While the pilot is lit, the burner responds to calls for heat from the thermostat or the remote transmitter.
Remote receiver box4 × AA
Hand-held transmitter2 × AAA

Place a wall thermostat in the same room as the insert, typically 5 feet off the floor and away from drafts.

Heads up: set to run on a thermostat, the insert may be very hot even when the burner doesn't seem to be on. Keep children away from it, and keep the transmitter where children can't reach it.

GI 645 DV MV: after seven days with no call for heat, the pilot goes out and must be relit by hand. For the remote's own buttons and features, see the instructions that come with the kit.

blower.title: Using the blower
blower.html:
The blower runs on 120 VAC household power. Its switch has Manual, AUTO and OFF positions.

ManualRuns whatever the firebox temperature, at the speed set by the knob on the switch panel. It stays on, burner or not, until you switch to AUTO or OFF.
AUTOTurns on when its thermostat reaches 140°F (60°C). After the burner shuts off, it keeps running until the firebox cools below 120°F.
  • The blower's three-prong plug goes straight into a properly grounded three-prong outlet. Never cut or remove the grounding prong.
  • A slight hum on low that grows as the fan speeds up is normal.
  • Always disconnect the power supply before any service on the insert.

care.title: Cleaning & yearly service
care.html:
Have the insert and its venting inspected by a qualified service technician before use and at least once a year.

Cleaning

Make sure the burner and firebox are cold before you vacuum.

  • Monthly: vacuum the controls area under the firebox, more often if there's pet hair around.
  • At least yearly: vacuum the firebox (more often with pets), using a flexible attachment to reach the valve compartment and blower area, and a soft brush attachment on the logs.
  • Remove any debris from the burner ports, especially the pilot carry-over ports.

Yearly checks

  • Glass gasket: look for wear or stiffness and make sure it still seals. A good seal keeps combustion gases out of the room.
  • Pilot assembly: check for corrosion, and have any damaged parts replaced by a qualified service technician.
Keep the area around the insert clear of anything that can burn, and of gasoline or other flammable liquids. Always disconnect electrical power before servicing.

safety.title: Safety & gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Put out any open flame and open windows.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Around the insert

  • Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • The safety screen barrier must stay installed. If it's damaged, replace it only with Jøtul part 226508 (steel overlay) or 226363 (cast iron overlay).
  • Supervise young children in the room. A child guard or safety gate is recommended if anyone at risk lives with you.
  • Keep furniture, drapes and clothing away, and never store gasoline or other flammable liquids nearby.
  • Burn only natural gas or propane, never wood, paper, cardboard or coal.
  • Don't use it if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the insert and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.
Massachusetts: a carbon monoxide detector must be installed in the same room as the insert.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Jøtul's limited warranty covers the original retail purchaser, from the date of purchase:

Cast iron, steel doors, surround components, firebox5 years
Burner, burner treatments, firebox panels2 years
Enamel finish (peeling or fading)2 years
Gas & electrical parts: controls, plumbing, valve, blower1 year

To make a claim

  • Keep your dated sales receipt as proof of purchase.
  • Contact your nearest authorized Jøtul dealer. Jøtul must receive notice of a possible defect within 60 days of when it was first discovered, or reasonably could have been.

What voids it or isn't covered

  • Installation or service by anyone other than an authorized installer, service agency or gas supplier, or not following the manual and local codes.
  • Parts that wear normally, such as gaskets, paint and glass (unless damaged by thermal stress).
  • Unauthorized modification, enamel damage from misuse, and damage in transit.
This is a summary, and the warranty is not transferable. The full terms are in the manual.

Test points on the front of the valve: A = inlet (supply), B = manifold (to the burner). Always test inlet pressure with the regulator control knob on HIGH and all other gas appliances in the residence on. An external regulator is needed for propane.

Don't allow inlet pressure to exceed 14.0" WC (or 1/2 PSIG): serious valve damage may result.

Low inlet pressure

  • Gas supply shut-off valve fully open?
  • Restriction in the fuel line?
  • Supply regulator set right for total household gas demand?
  • Gas line properly sized?

Low manifold pressure

  • Confirm correct inlet pressure.
  • Replace the regulator tower in the gas control valve.
  • Replace the valve.

  • The cast iron overlay covers a fireplace opening up to 26 3/8" high x 35 5/8" wide, with a 1/4" face overlap.
  • Choose a backer plate at least 1 inch larger than the fireplace opening.
  • Firebox width 33 1/2"; glass area 30 5/8" x 17 1/8". The other firebox dimensions are shown only in the fig. 5.1 drawing (p. 7).
  • Four corner leveling bolts give up to 1/2" of adjustment.
Don't modify the insert to make it fit: that voids the warranty, certifications and approvals and could be dangerous.

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
Vent through the chimney with a pair of 3" flexible aluminum liners listed for gas appliances, never into a chimney serving another appliance. Facing the insert, the intake collar is on the left and the exhaust on the right.

Cap height above unit10 ft (3.05 m) min · 35 ft (10.67 m) max
Liner diameter3"
Horizontal runsNot permitted
Liner endshang approx. 18 3/4" from the fireplace floor
  • Exhaust: full chimney length, connected directly to the termination cap.
  • Intake (U.S.): at least through the damper area into the first tile liner, or full length to the cap. Canada: both liners full length, connected to the unit and the termination kit.
  • Intake not connected to the cap: a block-off plate (noncombustible, p. 10; metal, pp. 12-13) above the unit, below the end of the intake, sealing the flue from the room; a direct vent cap is still required. Factory-built: at least a 6 foot length of intake flex into the flue.
  • Propane, vent runs over 10': a 4" exhaust liner is recommended, with the 3" intake run all the way to the vent terminus. 3" to 4" collar adaptors: ICC TM-L34; DuraVent 3GVBTI4 P/N 810004525.
  • A high-wind termination cap is recommended for all installs: M&G DuraVent Wind Screen #46DVA-VWG. "Prairie-style" caps are not recommended.
  • Use one listed manufacturer's components only (approved list, p. 36). Label the exhaust liner at both ends. The liner may not be exposed to any living space.
Using an existing chimney as the air intake isn't covered by the product certification test methods: consult the code authority having jurisdiction first.

specClear.title: Hearth & clearances
specClear.html:
Minimums for installing into a solid fuel-burning fireplace (figs. 5.3-5.6).

Hearth depth, unit flush12"
Hearth depth, unit raised min. 6"0"
Hearth width, unit raised min. 6"0"

Side room wall, from center line26 5/8"
Top trim from hearth (no shield / shield)46" / 38 1/2"
Ceiling from hearth surface64 3/4" min.

Hearth protection must be masonry material. On a raised hearth, forward protection may be reduced by two inches for every inch of fireplace floor elevation (fig. 5.4).

Note: the section 5.3 text on p. 8 says hearth protection must extend at least 3 1/8" to each side of the fireplace opening (and 12" forward from the facing material); the fig. 5.3 legend on the same page gives hearth protection width from the fireplace opening, unit flush, as min. 4 5/8".

"Fire resistant" materials and fire-rated sheet rock count as combustible. Keep clearances open for ventilation air around the insert.

specElec.title: Electrical
specElec.html:
Blower supply120 VAC
Plugthree-prong (grounding)
Blower157969 cross flow, 12" cage, 120 CFM
Snapstat140-120 °F, normally open
  • Ground the blower per local codes or, without them, ANSI/NFPA 70 (National Electrical Code) or CSA C22.1 (Canadian Electrical Code).
  • Plug directly into a properly grounded three-prong receptacle. Don't cut or remove the grounding prong.
  • Be aware of wiring locations when cutting holes in walls and ceilings for termination.
  • Always disconnect the power supply when servicing; label all wires before disconnecting control wiring.

Optional wall thermostat #750003: 750 millivolt, DC two-wire circuit; min. 16 gauge wire, max. 35 feet.

conflicts.issue: High-altitude (2000-4500 ft) maximum input: p. 15 gives 36100 NG / 34675 LP BTU/hr; the rating specifications in the fuel conversion section on p. 16 give 36,950 NG / 35,500 LP. Minimums agree (19,950 / 19,000).

Hearth protection width: section 5.3 text says masonry hearth protection extends at least 3 1/8" to each side of the fireplace opening (12" forward from the facing material); the fig. 5.3 legend gives hearth protection width from the opening, unit flush, min. 4 5/8" (depth 12" from the opening).

Ember material: p. 3 hardware kit lists Rock Wool Ember Fibers and pp. 23/25 say use rock wool fibers; p. 21 says use Ember Stones from the Miscellaneous Hardware bag (Ember Stones, 4 oz. listed with Traditional set 158153) and p. 26 fig. 7.40 says Burner Ember Stones are included in the Misc. Kit.
LP conversion Label A placement: kit contents list says apply to the base of the valve compartment; conversion step 7 says the right side compartment adjacent to the Rating Plate.

review.notes: Manual 139987 rev. 5 (7/22) covers two models, GI 645 DV and GI 645 DV MV (Astrid); the guide covers both and marks MV-only items (pilot shuts off after 7 days without a call for heat; Canadian efficiency). Catalog checks: BTU min/max, P.4.1 efficiency (63.03/62.56, which is the GI 645 DV; the DV MV is 64.55/64.57), 3" liners, view area (glass area 30 5/8" x 17 1/8"), width (firebox width 33 1/2" from the p. 7 power-cord note), mobile-home approval, blower and millivolt/standing-pilot ignition all agree. Height 23.75 and depth 16 appear only as unlabeled numbers in the fig. 5.1 drawing, so they were not confirmed or transcribed; weight (210 lb) and heating area (2,200 sq ft) are not in the manual. Certification: cover says ANSI Z21.88-2019 / CSA 2.33-2019 plus CAN/CGA 2.17-M17, p. 4 says CAN/CSA 2.17-2019 for high altitude; vent notices on pp. 10 and 12 cite older Z21.88-2014 / -1999 and CSA 2.33-M04 test methods. Shell lists only the two standards both pages agree on. Pressures given in in. WC only; the p. 4 kPa equivalents were left out because they are internally inconsistent (11.0 WC printed as 3.00 kPa for LP inlet and 2.99 kPa for LP manifold; NG inlet 5.0 WC shown as 1.00 kPa). Stale cross-references: the table of contents gives Operation 26, Warranty 35, Troubleshooting 36, Lighting 39 (physical pp. 28, 37, 38, 41); p. 16 points to the Initial System Check on page 26 (p. 28); p. 13 points to section 7.8 for the backer plate (it is on p. 19, numbered 7.4 there and 7.5 in the TOC); p. 18 cites fig. 10.1 page 30 and part #53 pg 33 (pp. 32, 35); p. 10 cites the Appendix on page 34 (p. 36). Section 5.3 hearth text names only the GI 645 DV MV. Backer plate slot letters on p. 19 disagree between the text and the fig. 7.8 callouts (B/C/D); the guide says outer slots (backer plate) and inner slots (overlay) without letters. The p. 8 backer plate list (158182 line) is garbled; sizes taken from p. 4. The LP kit contents list on p. 16 does not include a pilot injector although conversion step 5 installs one from the kit (parts list has LP pilot injector 226759); kit contents were not listed in the guide. Glass: p. 31 says use only PN 226451; parts list p. 35 item 24 is 158203 Glass w/ Gasket (possibly glass-only vs. with gasket). Massachusetts T-handle: p. 2 says an additional T-handle valve may be required, p. 14 says a T-handle gas cock is required (248 CMR); guide uses p. 14. Birch Log Set 158352 (pp. 25-26) is not in the p. 4 accessories list. Log placement is shown in photos; the guide does not transcribe log positions. Lighting instructions on p. 41 are printed in two interleaved columns; steps were read in numbered order (step 5 clockwise to OFF, step 9 counterclockwise to ON) and match the shutdown steps. p. 14's running header is in the 29-code-point offset font (decodes to the standard '139987-5 GI 645 DV and DV MV 7/22' header); a short heading above the assembly list ('6;598!  8786;59') does not decode with that rule and was ignored. No French-only safety text; the smell-gas block is in English on pp. 1 and 41. The manual does not say whether the burner works in a power outage (only that 120 VAC is needed for the blower), and remote button functions are in the kit's separate instructions, so neither is covered. Warranty p. 37 says repair or replace including parts & labor but also limits liability to the replacement component cost; the owner summary doesn't mention labor. No code table in the manual (codes: []).
